newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dollar rises to 111.21 yen, highest since Jan 1994.
newsitem.headline: Dollar rises to 111.21 yen, highest since Jan 1994.

text.p: The dollar rose to 111.21 yen in Tokyo afternoon trade on Monday, its highest level since January 1994, traders said.
The dollar got a jump start in Tokyo morning trade on Monday as market participants bought the U.S. currency for commercial purposes, traders said.

Traders said the bullish sentiment was helped by a meeting of Group of Seven (G7) finance ministers and central bank governors over the weekend, at which the policy makers said they "welcomed developments in exchange markets over the recent period", meaning the U.S. currency's recent strength.

Although this comment was nothing new in that it was similar in tone to recent remarks from G7 policy makers, it gave currency market participants the assurance to carry on buying the dollar, traders said.

They also said there was no incentive to buy the yen, with Japanese interest rates currently at record low levels. The yen has weakened from a record high of 79.75 to the dollar which it hit in April 1995.
